digest.overview: 今日条目集中在OLED与MicroLED两条主线：一方面围绕LTPO背板专利诉讼、蓝光PSF发光材料量产展示与透明OLED产品目录扩容，反映OLED在材料、器件与产品形态上的持续推进；另一方面ams OSRAM给出microLED共封装光学的商用时间表，显示MicroLED正探索数据中心互连等新场景。整体看，专利、材料效率与新型应用是今日信息的主要落点。

news.title_zh: Prevalent Display 就四项原属群创的 AMOLED 专利起诉三星
news.summary_zh: 美国非执业实体 Prevalent Display 在得克萨斯东区联邦法院起诉三星显示、三星电子及三星电子美国公司，称其 OLED 显示屏侵犯四项美国专利。这些专利原由台湾群创于 2015 至 2016 年申请、2026 年 4 月转让给 Prevalent，其中两项涉及 LTPS 驱动晶体管与氧化物半导体开关晶体管结合的混合晶体管 AMOLED 像素驱动电路，Prevalent 称其对应三星的 LTPO 背板技术。
news.why: LTPO 背板相关专利进入诉讼环节，可能影响采用混合氧化物与多晶硅技术的 OLED 面板厂商的专利风险与授权成本评估。

news.title_zh: ams OSRAM 预计首批 microLED 共封装光学约在 2029-2030 年商用，称其 AR microLED 收入已临近
news.summary_zh: ams OSRAM 在 2026 年第三季度财报电话会上，CEO Aldo Kamper 表示 microLED 共封装光学（CPO）的首批商用可能在 2029 或 2030 年，并称目前各方技术尚未就绪。公司为 AI 数据中心互连开发两种发射器技术，首款光互连产品将基于 850 nm 薄膜 microVCSEL，面向约 75 米以内链路，先从有源光缆起步，该平台在第三季度实现约 0.25 pJ/bit 下 32 Gb/s 无误码运行。
news.why: 为 MicroLED 在数据中心光互连的产业化节奏提供明确时间预期，也显示 microVCSEL 与 MicroLED 在短距互连场景中的并行布局。

news.title_zh: OLED Marketplace 收录达 200 款，京东方 48 英寸超宽透明 OLED 成为第 200 项
news.summary_zh: OLED-Info 的商用 OLED 显示屏免费目录 OLED Marketplace 达到 200 款收录，第 200 款为京东方 48 英寸超宽透明 OLED（BOE-TR-48）。该面板为 1920x540 分辨率、32:9 超宽比例，透明度 40%，最大亮度 400 尼特，刷新率 120 Hz，寿命超过 30000 小时，厚 1.4 mm、重 1.55 kg，已量产，适合橱窗、博物馆展陈、数字标牌与交通等场景。
news.why: 反映透明 OLED 已进入量产并拓展商用场景，目录扩容也为下游集成商选型提供更完整的商用面板清单。

news.title_zh: TCL 华星展示全球首款采用蓝色 PSF 发光体的 OLED 智能手机显示屏
news.summary_zh: TCL 华星在 DTC 2026 活动上展示首批采用 PSF 发光体的 OLED 显示屏，称其为面向智能手机或相机应用的全球首款蓝色磷光 OLED。展品包括 6.36 英寸手机屏和 2.86 英寸紧凑相机屏，蓝色子像素均基于 PSF（磷光敏化荧光）技术，华星称手机屏在同等亮度下比标准荧光蓝光方案功耗低 30%。PSF 体系中磷光材料作为敏化剂收集三线态激子并将能量传递给发出光的荧光蓝光发光体。
news.why: 蓝色发光效率与功耗是 OLED 的关键瓶颈，PSF 蓝光方案若落地有望降低手机 OLED 功耗，并推动蓝色磷光相关材料与器件路线竞争。

trends: OLED 材料与器件效率持续演进，蓝色发光方案（PSF）与 LTPO 背板成为关注焦点
专利与知识产权在 OLED 面板技术竞争中扮演重要角色，涉及 LTPO 等背板技术
MicroLED 正从显示向数据中心光互连等新应用延伸，但商用时间表仍偏后

items.title: Prevalent Display sues Samsung over four former Innolux AMOLED patents
items.abstract: US-based Prevalent Display LLC, an IP company (a non-practicing entity,. or NPE), has filed a lawsuit against Samsung Display , Samsung Electronics and Samsung Electronics America in the US District Court for the Eastern District of Texas. It claims that Samsung's OLED displays infringe four of its US patents. Prevalent did not develop these patents itself. They were first filed by Taiwan's Innolux in 2015 and 2016, and were assigned to Prevalent in April 2026. Two of the patents, US 10,902,775 and US 11,450,273 , cover an AMOLED pixel driving circuit with "hybrid transistors": low-temperature polysilicon (LTPS) drive transistors combined with an oxide semiconductor switching transistor. Prevalent says that this matches Samsung Display's LTPO backplane technology, which SDC calls HOP (Hybrid Oxide and Polycrystalline silicon). LTPO lets a display lower its refresh rate when it shows static content, such as a photo or an always-on clock, to save power, and raise it when the user plays a game.

items.title: ams OSRAM expects the first microLED co-packaged optics to be commercialized around 2029-2030, says its AR microLED revenue is close
items.abstract: ams OSRAM reported its financial results for Q3 2026, and during the earnings call CEO Aldo Kamper gave a timeline for the company's microLED-based optical interconnects. Kamper said that the first commercialization of microLED co-packaged optics (CPO) could come around 2029 or 2030 ("it is everybody's guess whether it is 2029 or 2030"), and not much earlier, "because neither we nor the other players have the technology ready to go right now". ams OSRAM now develops two emitter technologies for AI data-center interconnects. Its first optical interconnect product will be based on 850 nm thin-film microVCSELs, for links of up to about 75 meters, starting with active optical cables, which Kamper called a safe environment to try out new technologies. In Q3, the microVCSEL platform demonstrated error-free 32 Gb/s operation at about 0.25 pJ/bit. MicroLEDs, Kamper said, remain very relevant for links shorter than a meter where placing memory 30-40 centimeters away from the GPU would already be "a huge relief". Over such short distances, microLEDs are a lot more energy efficient than microVCSELs. This application is, however, much closer to co-packaged optics, which requires much more integration work and will take longer to materialize.

items.title: The OLED Marketplace reaches 200 displays with BOE's 48" ultra-wide transparent OLED as our 200th listing
items.abstract: We are happy to announce a milestone: the OLED Marketplace , OLED-Info's free catalog of commercial OLED displays, now lists 200 displays! Fittingly, the 200th panel is a large and unique one - BOE's 48" ultra-wide transparent OLED display (BOE-TR-48) . The BOE-TR-48 is a 48" panel with a 1920x540 resolution in an ultra-wide 32:9 aspect ratio, and a transparency of 40%. It offers a maximum luminance of 400 nits, a 120 Hz refresh rate and a lifetime of over 30,000 hours. The panel is only 1.4 mm thick and weighs 1.55 kg. The display is in mass production, and its long, narrow format makes it well suited for shop windows and showcases, museum exhibits, digital signage and transportation applications.

items.title: TCL CSOT shows world's first OLED smartphone displays with blue PSF emitters
items.abstract: TCL CSOT showed its first PSF emitter powered OLED displays at its DTC 2026 event. The company says that these are the world's first blue phosphorescent OLEDs for smartphone or camera applications. The displays are a 6.36-inch smartphone display and a 2.86-inch display for compact cameras. Both are based on PSF (Phosphor-Sensitized Fluorescence) technology for the blue subpixel, and CSOT says that the phone display uses 30% less power at the same brightness than a display with a standard fluorescent blue. In a PSF system the phosphorescent material is not the emitter. It acts as a sensitizer that harvests the triplet excitons and hands their energy over to a fluorescent blue emitter, which produces the light. The device can use all of the excitons, while the light itself comes from a fluorescent molecule with a fast, nanosecond-scale emission.
